answer: One concrete mechanism: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because pigment only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, jade is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any ember approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
